title: Adult-Onset Still's Disease and Septic Arthritis

questions.sec: Adult-onset Still's disease phenotype, triad and Yamaguchi major criteria
questions.q: What age band and form of presentation are printed for adult-onset Still's disease?
opts: No defined age with skin-limited disease
25–45 years with systemic form of presentation
questions.exp: Adult Onset Still's Disease: age 25–45 yrs; systemic form of presentation. (Book p552)

questions.sec: Adult-onset Still's disease phenotype, triad and Yamaguchi major criteria
questions.q: What prodromal phase feature is printed for AOSD?
questions.exp: Features: prodromal phase — sore throat. (Book p552)

questions.sec: Adult-onset Still's disease phenotype, triad and Yamaguchi major criteria
questions.q: How is the fever component of the clinical triad described?
opts: Persistent high spiking fever that reaches subnormal levels during the day (quotidian pattern)
questions.exp: Clinical triad: fever — persistent high spiking reaches subnormal levels during day (quotidian). (Book p552)

questions.sec: Adult-onset Still's disease phenotype, triad and Yamaguchi major criteria
questions.q: What rash morphology and behavior are printed in the triad?
questions.exp: Salmon colored rash: transient evanescent maculo papular rash. (Book p552)

questions.sec: Adult-onset Still's disease phenotype, triad and Yamaguchi major criteria
questions.q: What arthritis distribution and site order are printed for AOSD?
opts: Symmetric polyarticular with knee greater than wrist greater than ankle greater than elbow
questions.exp: Arthritis: symmetric, polyarticular (knee greater than wrist greater than ankle greater than elbow). (Book p552)

questions.sec: Adult-onset Still's disease phenotype, triad and Yamaguchi major criteria
questions.q: What percentage progresses to severe or destructive arthritis, and where are erosions most common?
opts: 25% severe/destructive arthritis; joint erosions most common in children
questions.exp: Progress to severe/destructive arthritis in 25% of cases; joint erosions m/c in children. (Book p552)

questions.sec: Adult-onset Still's disease phenotype, triad and Yamaguchi major criteria
questions.q: Which cluster is labelled bad prognosis in AOSD?
opts: Sore throat and salmon rash alone
questions.exp: Serositis, lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly are bracketed as bad prognosis. (Book p552)

questions.sec: Adult-onset Still's disease phenotype, triad and Yamaguchi major criteria
questions.q: Which blood parameters are printed for AOSD?
opts: Normal white count with high albumin
Leukocytosis, raised ESR, raised CRP, raised ferritin and low serum albumin
questions.exp: Blood parameters: leukocytosis; ESR increased; CRP increased; ferritin increased; S. albumin decreased. (Book p552)

questions.sec: Adult-onset Still's disease phenotype, triad and Yamaguchi major criteria
questions.q: What score threshold and four major criteria items are printed for Yamaguchi criteria?
opts: Greater than 3 with sore throat only
Greater than 10 including organomegaly as major
Greater than 5; fever over 39°C for 7 days, arthritis/arthralgia for 2 weeks, rash and leukocytosis
questions.exp: Yamaguchi criteria (greater than 5): major — fever (>39°C) for 7 days; arthritis/arthralgia for 2 weeks; rash; leukocytosis. (Book p552)

questions.sec: Yamaguchi minor criteria, HLH, AOSD therapy and septic-arthritis foundations
questions.q: Which items are printed as Yamaguchi minor criteria?
opts: Sore throat; negative ANA and RF; hepatosplenomegaly with lymphadenopathy; abnormal ALT/AST
questions.exp: minor: sore throat; negative ANA, RF; hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy; abnormal ALT/AST. (Book p553)

questions.sec: Yamaguchi minor criteria, HLH, AOSD therapy and septic-arthritis foundations
questions.q: How is hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis introduced relative to AOSD?
opts: Rheumatological emergency seen in 10% of AOSD
questions.exp: HLH: rheumatological emergency; seen in 10% of AOSD. (Book p553)

questions.sec: Yamaguchi minor criteria, HLH, AOSD therapy and septic-arthritis foundations
questions.q: Which feature set with directions is printed for HLH?
opts: Pancytopenia, unsubsiding fever, very high ferritin, low ESR, low fibrinogen and high triglycerides
questions.exp: Features: pancytopenia; ESR decreased; unsubsiding fever; fibrinogen decreased; ferritin increased increased; triglycerides increased. (Book p553)

questions.sec: Yamaguchi minor criteria, HLH, AOSD therapy and septic-arthritis foundations
questions.q: Which complications follow the HLH block?
opts: Bleeding from thrombocytopenia, transient thrombocytopenic purpura, DIC with consumptive coagulopathy and AA amyloidosis
questions.exp: Complications: bleeding d/t thrombocytopenia; transient thrombocytopenic purpura; DIC with consumptive coagulopathy; AA amyloidosis. (Book p553)

questions.sec: Yamaguchi minor criteria, HLH, AOSD therapy and septic-arthritis foundations
questions.q: How is steroid therapy sequenced in AOSD according to the printed note?
questions.exp: Treatment: steroid — pulse therapy then oral therapy. (Book p553)

questions.sec: Yamaguchi minor criteria, HLH, AOSD therapy and septic-arthritis foundations
questions.q: What is the printed step-up ladder for AOSD treatment?
opts: Mild: NSAID; no response → steroid plus methotrexate; then anti IL-1 and IL-6
Methotrexate first with no NSAID step
questions.exp: Treatment of AOSD: mild — NSAID; no response → steroid + methotrexate → anti IL-1, IL-6. (Book p553)

questions.sec: Yamaguchi minor criteria, HLH, AOSD therapy and septic-arthritis foundations
questions.q: Which drug is explicitly avoided in AOSD?
questions.exp: Note: sulfasalazine is avoided. (Book p553)

questions.sec: Yamaguchi minor criteria, HLH, AOSD therapy and septic-arthritis foundations
questions.q: Which hosts are listed as susceptible to acute monoarticular septic arthritis?
opts: Children, elderly, immunocompromised and IV drug abusers (oligo/polyarticular)
questions.exp: Susceptible host: children, elderly; immunocompromised; IV drug abuse (oligo/polyarticular). (Book p553)

questions.sec: Yamaguchi minor criteria, HLH, AOSD therapy and septic-arthritis foundations
questions.q: What clinical presentation is printed for septic arthritis?
opts: Fever, pain with limited range of motion (most common knee) and no history of similar episodes
questions.exp: Clinical presentation: fever; pain + limited range of motion (m/c: knee); no h/o similar episode. (Book p553)

questions.sec: Yamaguchi minor criteria, HLH, AOSD therapy and septic-arthritis foundations
questions.q: What infection percentage, organism hierarchy and spread route are printed?
opts: Infection 20%: Staphylococcus aureus greater than Streptococcus pneumoniae greater than Gram-negative bacillus; spread hematogenous
questions.exp: Causes: infection (20%) — staph. aureus greater than strep. pneumonia greater than gram-negative bacillus; spread: hematogenous. (Book p553)

questions.sec: Yamaguchi minor criteria, HLH, AOSD therapy and septic-arthritis foundations
questions.q: Which non-infectious causes are listed among acute monoarticular arthritis mimics?
opts: Crystal deposition with sterile cultures only
Trauma, tumour, osteoarthritis of a single joint and sarcoidosis
questions.exp: Other causes: trauma; tumour; osteoarthritis of single joint; sarcoidosis. (Book p553)

questions.sec: Gonococcal versus septic comparison, septic-arthritis management and arthritis approach
questions.q: Which differentials are first printed to be ruled out before labeling monoarticular arthritis as septic?
opts: Tendinitis and bursitis; hemophilia as a similar presentation
questions.exp: D/d: tendinitis, bursitis to be ruled out; hemophilia — similar presentation. (Book p554)

questions.sec: Gonococcal versus septic comparison, septic-arthritis management and arthritis approach
questions.q: In the gonococcal versus septic table, which host and pattern row is correct?
opts: Gonococcal: young healthy with migratory polyarthralgia/arthritis; septic: immunocompromised with monoarticular arthritis
Both occur only in healthy athletes
questions.exp: Table: host — gonococcal young healthy versus septic immunocompromised; pattern — migratory polyarthralgia/arthritis versus monoarticular arthritis. (Book p554)

questions.sec: Gonococcal versus septic comparison, septic-arthritis management and arthritis approach
questions.q: Which feature favors gonococcal infection over septic arthritis in the printed table?
opts: Tenosynovitis and skin rash present; good prognosis with lower joint/blood culture yield
Higher culture yield and poor prognosis
questions.exp: Tenosynovitis + and skin rash + favor gonococcal, with less culture yield and good prognosis versus septic negative for both, more yield and poor prognosis. (Book p554)

questions.sec: Gonococcal versus septic comparison, septic-arthritis management and arthritis approach
questions.q: What is the gold-standard diagnostic test and WBC threshold printed for septic arthritis?
opts: Plain x-ray alone with normal WBC
Synovial fluid analysis with WBC greater than 50,000 per microlitre
questions.exp: Diagnosis: synovial fluid analysis — gold standard; WBC greater than 50000 /μL. (Book p554)

questions.sec: Gonococcal versus septic comparison, septic-arthritis management and arthritis approach
questions.q: Which antibiotic pair and drainage indications are printed for septic arthritis?
opts: No antibiotics with aspiration alone always
Vancomycin plus ceftriaxone; drain for thick pus or shoulder/hip involvement
questions.exp: Rx: antibiotics — vancomycin + ceftriaxone; drainage indications — thick pus; shoulder, hip joint involvement. (Book p554)

questions.sec: Gonococcal versus septic comparison, septic-arthritis management and arthritis approach
questions.q: Which causes of chronic monoarticular arthritis are listed?
opts: TB, fungal disease, Lyme disease, sarcoidosis, spondyloarthritis and non-inflammatory causes
questions.exp: Chronic monoarticular arthritis causes: TB; fungal disease; Lyme; sarcoidosis; spondyloarthritis; non-inflammatory. (Book p554)

questions.sec: Gonococcal versus septic comparison, septic-arthritis management and arthritis approach
questions.q: How does the printed approach tree first split arthritis?
questions.exp: Approach to arthritis begins with monoarticular arthritis and polyarticular arthritis branches. (Book p554)

questions.sec: Gonococcal versus septic comparison, septic-arthritis management and arthritis approach
questions.q: What sub-branches follow monoarticular and polyarticular arthritis in the flowchart?
opts: Monoarticular → septic and crystal; polyarticular → acute (undifferentiated, post-viral) and chronic inflammatory (RA with d/d SLE, psoriatic arthritis)
Monoarticular → septic only; polyarticular → OA only
questions.exp: Monoarticular branches septic and crystal; polyarticular branches acute (undifferentiated, post viral) and chronic inflammatory: RA with d/d SLE and psoriatic arthritis. (Book p554)

units.title: 1. Adult-onset Still's disease phenotype, triad and Yamaguchi major criteria
units.sec: Adult-onset Still's disease phenotype, triad and Yamaguchi major criteria
units.guide:
Age, systemic presentation and sore-throat prodrome open the chapter. The fever–salmon-rash–polyarthritis triad with destructive 25% risk and poor-prognosis signs follow.
Blood parameters and Yamaguchi major items are kept in printed order.

units.title: 2. Yamaguchi minor criteria, HLH, AOSD therapy and septic-arthritis foundations
units.sec: Yamaguchi minor criteria, HLH, AOSD therapy and septic-arthritis foundations
units.guide:
Minor criteria and lab abnormalities finish Yamaguchi. HLH as 10% rheumatologic emergency with cytopenia and coagulation features follows.
NSAID→steroid/MTX→anti-IL ladder, sulfasalazine avoidance and septic hosts/causes close the unit.

units.title: 3. Gonococcal versus septic comparison, septic-arthritis management and arthritis approach
units.sec: Gonococcal versus septic comparison, septic-arthritis management and arthritis approach
units.guide:
Tendinitis/bursitis and hemophilia d/d plus the gonococcal–septic table open the final unit. Synovial-fluid gold standard, WBC threshold and antibiotic/drainage rules follow.
Chronic monoarticular causes and the mono-versus-poly approach tree close Chapter 29.
